Short answer: Toast is built around restaurant operations. Clover is a broader POS platform sold through different providers. A bar should test its real rush workflow and the exact reseller contract before choosing.

What this means for your business

The logo on the terminal is not the whole system. Hardware, payment processing, apps, support, network, contract, replacement timing, and closeout all matter when the room is full.

What to watch

  • A quote that leaves out processor, reseller, app, hardware, or support terms.
  • Tabs, tips, modifiers, printers, or offline steps skipped in the demo.
  • Support responsibility split among several companies.
  • A cutover scheduled without staff training or fallback.

Do this next

  1. Write ten ugly rush-hour orders and the nightly close.
  2. Run them on the exact hardware and plan quoted.
  3. Read payment, term, cancellation, support, and replacement terms.
  4. Document network, offline, cash, and escalation procedures.

When Little Fight fits

We help NYC venues map, test, network, and document the complete setup. We do not sell either POS and will not declare a winner from a feature grid.
